title: No structure exists solely for the good of another species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: No structure exists solely for the good of another species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Natural selection cannot produce any structure in one species exclusively for the good of another species, though it can produce structures that harm other species; proof of such a structure would refute the theory.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Natural selection cannot possibly produce any modification in any one species exclusively for the good of another species

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Organs of small importance.”. Scope: all interacting species

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.39

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public data can identify candidate mutualisms or exploitative structures but seldom measure all fitness consequences. The universal negative cannot be confirmed exhaustively.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Catalogue interspecific traits and estimate their direct and inclusive-fitness effects on the bearer and beneficiary. A trait with persistent benefit only to another species and no direct or indirect benefit to its bearer would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exclusive absence of bearer benefit is extremely hard to establish.

Interaction databases rarely contain fitness effects.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The refuting observation is well defined, but the variable that would show it, exclusive fitness benefit, is not a field in open interaction databases and is only scattered through experimental papers. GloBI can list mutualisms and antagonisms to examine, which is a partial screen. Coverage across all interacting species is negligible relative to the scope, and compilation would take far longer than weeks.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For structures involved in interspecific interactions, compare fitness effects on the bearer and on the other species. One structure whose only effect is a benefit to another species, with no benefit to the bearer or its kin, would refute the claim; a survey that finds return benefits in candidate mutualisms supports it only weakly.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cryptic return benefits and parasite manipulation are hard to separate from a structure evolved for another species.

Interaction records do not contain fitness effects or exclusive beneficiaries.

A universal negative cannot be confirmed by failing to find a case.
